new_statements.rule_in_words: Laughren analyses Palaka not as a straightforwardly tonal language but as an accentual one: each word has an accented syllable, realised with high pitch, and the inherited Senufo tone contrast has been reinterpreted as a high (accented) vs. low (unaccented) opposition. The accessible text does not say which syllable carries the accent (no rule such as initial/final is visible), and her 1977 article adds only that the tone (pitch pattern) of a Palaka noun stem appears invariable under determination, i.e. the accent seems to be a fixed property of the stem rather than assigned by phrase-level rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing visible in the accessible snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: None visible; Laughren flags that the tone/accent marks in her 2001 Palaka data are provisional.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (lexical stems); statement is the author's summary of her own earlier fieldwork analysis (Laughren 1977a, b), given as background in a vowel-harmony paper. Accessed only as Google Books snippets; the words immediately preceding 'the tonal system of Palaka' (probably a self-citation) were not recovered because Google refused further search-within requests (not reachable by automated download 'automated queries') for the rest of the session.
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern Palaka proper (self-name pilára / plára, 'Kpalaga'), spoken in c. 23 villages east of Ferkessédougou, Côte d'Ivoire = Glottolog pala1342 / ISO plr; Laughren's data are from her own 1970s fieldwork there. Not to be confused with WALS code 'plr' (= Palor, a Cangin language of Senegal, palo1243), which surfaced in the local WALS files. The Mills 1984 first-syllable stress rule held by the project belongs to Cebaara/Tyebaara (ceba1235), not Palaka.

sources.citation: Mills, Elizabeth. 1984. Senoufo phonology, discourse to syllable (a prosodic approach). SIL Publications in Linguistics 72. Dallas: SIL / University of Texas at Arlington. (Glottolog cites pp. xii-xx for Palaka.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Cebaara (Tyebaara of Korhogo), not Palaka. Front matter mentions Palaka only for classification: 'Palakas are a small group east of Ferkessédougou whose language is different enough to be considered a distinct language of the Senoufo group'; Palaka 'seems to be a separate division'; Palaka has x where Senari has glottal stop. Its stress statement ('Stress always occurs on the first syllable of the basic word', p.119) applies to Tyebaara only.
